protocol: HTTPS only; REST with JSON request and response bodies unless noted

versioning.strategy: Major version in the URL path (/v1); additive fields are backward-compatible within a major version. Deprecations provide a Sunset header and at least 90 days notice.
versioning.compatibility: Clients must ignore unknown response fields; breaking changes are released at /v2.

authentication.authorization: Every conversation, message, profile, and file operation is scoped to the authenticated subject. Return 404 rather than exposing resources owned by another user.

endpoints.description: Persist a user message, resolve server-side conversation context, and invoke the selected model. Set stream=true to receive tokens immediately as SSE.

request_schema.model: string (optional; allow-listed model ID, default server policy)
request_schema.max_tokens: integer (optional, 1-4096, capped by model and user quota)
request_schema.file_ids: array<uuid> (optional, max 10; must be owned by caller and ready)
request_schema.idempotency_key: string (optional, 8-128 characters; prevents duplicate persisted turns)

status_codes.422: Content rejected by validation or safety policy

example_request.message: Compare the two phones I uploaded.

message.content: I can compare their display, camera, and price.

endpoints.streaming_format: SSE when Accept: text/event-stream or stream=true. The initial HTTP status is 200; do not buffer model output.

endpoints.description: Create a conversation. Context is managed by storing messages by conversation_id; the server applies a token-aware recent-message window plus compacted summaries when serving /chat.

request_schema.title: string (optional, 1-120 characters)
request_schema.metadata: object (optional, max 10 KB; no secrets or raw credentials)

endpoints.description: List the caller's conversations using stable cursor pagination.
Return a chronological page of persisted messages for one conversation. Cursor pagination is preferred over offset pagination to prevent duplicates when new turns arrive.

query_params.before: opaque message cursor (optional; returns older messages)

endpoints.description: Retrieve a single message and its metadata.
Edit an eligible user-authored message. Editing creates a new revision and marks any dependent assistant completion stale; it never overwrites audit history.
Soft-delete a caller-owned message. The response body is removed from normal history while minimal encrypted audit metadata is retained under the data-retention policy.
Retrieve the current user's profile. Never return password hashes, JWTs, provider credentials, or raw sensitive attributes.

Upload a context file using multipart/form-data. Accepted types: application/pdf, text/plain, text/markdown, image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp. Files are virus-scanned, MIME-sniffed, encrypted at rest, and asynchronously extracted before they may be attached to /chat.

streaming_implementation.format: Server-Sent Events (SSE); WebSocket is optional only for bidirectional features such as cancellation and presence.
streaming_implementation.resume: Clients retain Last-Event-ID and may reconnect to GET /chat/streams/{stream_id}; replay is available for 10 minutes.

validation: Reject unknown model IDs, invalid UUIDs, oversized arrays/files, malformed JSON, empty or overlong strings, and invalid cursor signatures.
Normalize Unicode, trim message text, apply prompt-injection and abuse checks before model dispatch, and validate referenced resources belong to the caller.
data_protection: Encrypt message content, extracted file text, embeddings, and PII at rest using managed KMS envelope encryption; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
Store only keyed hashes for searchable sensitive identifiers where possible; redact secrets from logs, traces, model prompts, and error details.
Use signed short-lived download URLs and per-user authorization for files. Apply configurable retention/deletion policies and audit access without storing raw content in audit logs.
validation_and_privacy.performance: Keep profile/history/list endpoints under 200 ms p95 via indexed tenant-scoped queries, Redis caches, and cursor pagination. /chat begins streaming as soon as the provider emits a token; non-streaming /chat cannot guarantee <200 ms because model inference is external.

rate_limiting.algorithm: Redis-backed token bucket keyed by authenticated user ID, with IP-based pre-auth limits; return RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset, and Retry-After headers.

limits.POST /chat: 30 requests/minute and 120,000 requested tokens/hour per user

documentation_tool: OpenAPI 3.1 published as /v1/openapi.json and rendered by Swagger UI at /v1/docs; this document is the human-readable contract source.
testing_scenarios: Valid non-streaming chat and SSE delta-to-completed ordering
Invalid JWT, cross-tenant resource access, malformed UUID, and prompt-injection rejection
Idempotent retry and optimistic message-edit conflict
File type, size, malware, ownership, and extraction-status enforcement
Cursor pagination while new conversation messages arrive
Per-endpoint rate and token quota limits
100+ concurrent SSE clients with disconnect/reconnect and provider failure
Encryption/redaction assertions for persistence, logs, and telemetry

implementation_stack.framework: Any standards-compliant REST server (FastAPI, Express, Django, Go, Java, or similar)
implementation_stack.database: PostgreSQL with tenant-scoped indexes and encrypted application fields
implementation_stack.cache: Redis for rate limits, cursors, stream replay, and short-lived context cache
implementation_stack.queue: Durable worker queue for file scanning, extraction, embedding, summarization, and retryable provider work
implementation_stack.object_storage: Private encrypted S3-compatible storage for original files
